quota.py:4 uses strict '>' so current + requested == max_allowed grants; test_quota.py:7-11 (within quota) and test_quota.py:13-16 (over quota); runtime probe allocate('t1', 5, 5, 10) -> {'granted': 5, 'reason': 'ok', 'remaining': 0} confirms the inclusive boundary

findings.claim: The test suite does not exercise the equality boundary current + requested == max_allowed, so an off-by-one implementation that denies equality would pass all tests
evidence: no test case satisfies current + requested == max_allowed
findings.failure_mechanism: mutate quota.py:4 from '>' to '>=' -> allocate('t1',5,5,10) denied with 'over_quota' instead of granted -> all existing tests still pass while A2's inclusive-grant requirement is violated
findings.rejection_reason: test-strength on correct code — quota.py:4 uses strict '>' so equality grants, verified by reading and by runtime probe allocate('t1',5,5,10) -> {'granted': 5, 'reason': 'ok', 'remaining': 0}; no contract behavior is broken

findings.claim: The response-shape assertion is only applied to the success branch, so a mutation that adds extra keys or drops remaining in the unauthorized/over_quota branches would pass all tests
evidence: test_quota.py:23-25 checks the key set only on the success path
test_quota.py:18-21 and test_quota.py:13-17 assert only granted and reason on the error paths
findings.failure_mechanism: add an internal-counter key or drop remaining in an error-branch return -> error-path tests still pass because they read only granted/reason, and the shape test still passes because it checks only the success path -> R3's exact-shape rule violated without test failure
findings.rejection_reason: test-strength on correct code — all three return paths (quota.py:3,5,9) return exactly {granted, reason, remaining} with int values, verified by reading and by runtime probes on each path

findings.claim: test_quota.py omits the equality boundary current + requested == max_allowed, leaving A2/R2 untested for the inclusive grant case
evidence: no test case satisfies current + requested == max_allowed
findings.failure_mechanism: changing quota.py:4 from '>' to '>=' would still pass all existing tests while silently denying the boundary case A2 requires to grant with reason 'ok'
findings.rejection_reason: duplicate of tests-01 (same root cause: missing equality-boundary test) and test-strength on correct code — the inclusive boundary at quota.py:4 is verified correct by reading and runtime probe

findings.claim: Negative current input bypasses quota enforcement, allowing allocate to grant resources far beyond max_allowed
evidence: quota.py:4-9 performs current + requested > max_allowed without sign validation
findings.failure_mechanism: caller supplies negative current -> current + requested <= max_allowed holds -> full requested granted with inflated remaining, defeating the intended cap
findings.rejection_reason: contradicted by the contract — R2's literal rule (grant iff current + requested <= max_allowed) is satisfied for every input including negative current, and the contract states no non-negativity or input-validation constraint, so no requirement, invariant, or preserved behavior is violated; the claim critiques the contract's specified rule, not the implementation's conformance to it

minimum_next_action: None required — the implementation satisfies every contract requirement and invariant, and no validated finding changes the verdict
